record.paper_title: 1-Bend 3-D Orthogonal Box-Drawings: Two Open Problems Solved
record.original_question: For three-dimensional orthogonal graph drawings in which each edge route has at most three bends, what is the correct asymptotic lower bound on the required volume; specifically, for graphs of maximum degree Δ on n vertices, does every graph admit such a drawing of volume O(Δ n^1.5), which would match the known Ramanujan-graph lower bound Ω(Δ n^1.5)?

evidence.quote: What is the correct lower bound for 3-bend drawings? There are drawings of size O(n2.5) for Kn [BSWW99], and this is optimal [BSWW99]. For Ramanujan-graphs, the lower bound is Ω(∆n1.5) [BTW01], but it is not known whether every graph has a 3-bend drawing of volume O(∆n1.5).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A 3-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing of a graph G = (V, E) places each vertex v as an axis-aligned box in the integer grid Z^3 and routes each edge as a polyline composed of axis-parallel segments connecting points on the surfaces of the boxes of its endpoints, such that distinct edge routes are interior-disjoint and each edge route has at most a prescribed number of bends. The volume of such a drawing is the number of unit cells of the smallest axis-aligned bounding box.

Consider drawings in which every edge has at most 3 bends. For graphs G on n vertices with maximum degree Δ, determine the correct asymptotic lower bound on the volume required by any such 3-bend drawing. In particular, decide whether every graph of maximum degree Δ on n vertices admits a 3-bend 3-dimensional orthogonal box-drawing of volume O(Δ · n^{3/2}), thereby matching the known lower bound Ω(Δ · n^{3/2}) attained by Ramanujan graphs.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returns the same problem area but no result establishing an O(Δ n^{3/2}) volume upper bound for 3-bend 3D orthogonal drawings of arbitrary bounded-degree graphs. Best known constructions give larger volume (e.g., n^3+o(n^3) for general 3-bend drawings, n^{2.5} for K_n), while the Ω(Δ n^{3/2}) Ramanujan-graph lower bound stands. The matching upper bound appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: 1-bend 3-D orthogonal box-drawings: Two open problems solved
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bend/volume tradeoffs in 3D orthogonal box-drawings and lists the 3-bend lower bound question.
status_evidence.claim: The matching upper bound for 3-bend drawings is posed as an unresolved question.

status_evidence.title: Three-Dimensional Orthogonal Graph Drawing with Optimal Volume
status_evidence.snippet: 3-BENDS algorithm produces 3-bend drawings with n^3+o(n^3) volume, the best known upper bound for 3-bend 3D orthogonal drawings.
status_evidence.claim: Best known general upper bound for 3-bend drawings is far from O(Δ n^{1.5}).
